synopsis: Across the corpus, no credibility framework supplies a universal simulation-to-test tolerance or physical-test percentage; acceptance must reflect model influence, decision consequence, applicability and uncertainty [f187, f7535, f14577]. Sector-specific numbers are precedents, not off-road defaults: FAA seat guidance uses 10% tolerances that must not be copied to braking, while Euro NCAP VT v1.00 (2025) requires at least 75% qualification per verification-test cluster but leaves several ISO-score and KPI tolerances provisional [f7537, f14668, f2627, f2628, f2503]. The off-road evidence gap remains material: no sensor-simulation fidelity thresholds were found, few realism studies predefine acceptance thresholds, and documented terrain-model capabilities do not establish machine-specific stopping-distance accuracy [f5220, f5764, f4839, f6016]. The programme should pre-agree tolerances and metrics, distinguish advisory, urgent-warning, speed-reduction and full-braking interventions, and bound its conclusions by operating regime and configuration [f9930, f2634, f9934]. A narrow simulated clearance is not a robust pass when uncertainty is comparable to the safety margin; reference measurements must be substantially more precise than acceptance margins, and reports should carry tolerances alongside results [f4343, f14013, f7473, f4344]. The example roadmap places initial checks in December–January, a correlation campaign in February–March and a threshold decision at an April gate; failed calibration criteria, excessive stopping-distance residuals or tolerances beyond production capability should trigger recalibration, stopping or escalation [f9872, f6422, f10942, f10945].
